thread:
PagerDuty Bot: P1 ALERT - inference queue growth detected in us-west-2 (cluster: infer-usw2). queue_length > 500 for 5m, median latency > 120s. Incident ID INC-2026-0314-01. Paging on-call.

Infra Bot: Autoscaler attempted scale to 28 nodes but failed to stabilize; recent node registration timeouts and immediate NotReady -> cordon events observed. Recent node logs show repeated CUDA/Xid errors and kernel OOM messages on nodes p-infer-12, p-infer-15, p-infer-18. Sample log snippet: `GPU0: Xid 13, process redwood-runtime (pid 2345) killed by OOM`.

Alice K: I'm the on-call. Acknowledging, jumping in. @Tash (SRE) can you grab dmesg / nvidia logs from p-infer-12 and p-infer-15? @Carol R please start a short CS blurb for affected customers. Will start mitigation plan in thread.

Tash (SRE): I'm SSHing now to p-infer-12. dmesg shows repeated GPU fault entries and then `redwood-runtime` segfaults. `journalctl -u redwood-runtime` shows OOM_kill of the process repeatedly, and then kubelet marks the node NotReady after driver resets. Notably, node bootstrap logs show a driver install step: `nvidia-driver v525 -> v530` ran in the last image bake. New nodes come up with v525 but the kernel module on some hosts expects v530 -> version mismatch yields instability.

Tash (SRE): Quick findings:
- `Xid 13` (GPU page fault) correlated with `redwood-runtime` memory growth until OOM.
- Nodes with recent kernel/driver bump are flapping; others stable.
- Autoscaler sees flaps and keeps provisioning new nodes, which then fail similarly -> churn.

Alice K: Proposed mitigations (short):
1) Pause cluster-autoscaler to stop churn.
2) Set routing to prefer Dedicated/Reserved pools for production traffic (failover).
3) Cordon/flank test one flappy node and restart runtime to confirm quick recovery.
4) Roll back the driver version on the problematic AMI or push a matching kernel module to stop new nodes flapping.

Carol R: Draft CS status: "We are investigating increased latencies and intermittent errors for inference in us-west-2. A subset of GPU nodes are experiencing driver/runtime instability causing elevated queueing and occasional 429s. Engineers are mitigating, and we'll update every 30 minutes. Affected customers may see degraded throughput and transient errors."

Tash (SRE): Executing step 1 and 3 now. Commands run:
```bash
kubectl cordon p-infer-15
kubectl drain p-infer-15 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
ssh ec2-user@p-infer-12 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime && sudo dmesg | tail -n 50'
```
After restart on p-infer-12: queue on shard-4 dropped ~40% within 3 minutes, no new Xid entries on that node for 6m. However new nodes still failing to register due to driver kernel mismatch.

Infra Bot: Autoscaler status: paused by alice_k at 1758294620. Reserved pool capacity available: +6 reserved GPU machines. Routing updated to move ~30% traffic to reserved pool (policy change id: route-2026-0314-1). We can temporarily increase dedicated capacity if needed.

Tash (SRE): Root cause hypothesis: AMI bake introduced nvidia-driver v530 while some host kernels still expect v525 (or vice versa) — driver incompatible combos lead to GPU faults under load. Additionally, recent runtime memory growth exposes the driver sensitivity -> OOM -> Xid -> node teardown. Repro steps in staging show similar runtime memory growth when running large-batch inference.

Alice K: Next actions:
- Tash: coordinate with eng-infra to roll back AMI to v525 on us-west-2 single AZs, patch bootstrap script to lock driver version.
- Infra: provision 4 reserved nodes into routing pool to soak traffic while we stabilize.
- Carol: post CS update using draft and link status page.
- I'll hand off to Bob for the next shift at 06:00 UTC.

Bob M: I'm taking the handoff. Summary for next on-call:
- Incident ID: INC-2026-0314-01, P1.
- Timeline: alert at 1758294321 -> autoscaler paused 1758294620 -> cordon/drain and runtime restarts 1758294700-1758294900.
- Mitigations in place: autoscaler paused, routing shifted to reserved pool, driver rollback in progress (AMI rollback queued), temporary +6 reserved GPUs added.
- Ongoing tasks: validate AMI rollback across AZs, monitor queue length and Xid events, gradually re-enable autoscaler once stable for 30m, coordinate postmortem once resolved.
- Pager/contact: Bob M (primary), Tash (SRE) (secondary), Alice K (creator).

Bob M: executing validation scripts now. `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer` shows 6 nodes ready in routing pool, 3 nodes cordoned. No new Xid events in last 10m on rolled-back nodes.

CS Bot: Status update posted to customers at 1758295000: "Investigating increased latencies and intermittent errors in us-west-2. Mitigation underway. Next update in 30 minutes."

Tash (SRE): Observed log after AMI rollback on two test nodes: `dmesg` shows no new GPU page faults under sustained load for 12m. Runtime memory allocation still high for specific long-running requests; will open a runtime memory profiling ticket (ENG-RUNTIME-1427).

Alice K: Good work. If no Xid events and queue length drops under 100 for 30m, we'll re-enable autoscaler with conservative limits (max surge 4 nodes) and keep routing policy sticky to reserved pool 15% for an hour.

Bob M: Taking over monitoring. Next update +20m or earlier on any regressions. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
